chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Al-Kalalah is one who has no parent and no child."

key_terms.اَلْكَلاَلَةُ: Kalalah: A legal term for a deceased person with no direct ascendants or descendants.
key_terms.وَالِدٌ: Parent/Ascendant: Refers to father or mother.
key_terms.وَلَدٌ: Child/Descendant: Refers to son or daughter.

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Kalalah in Shia inheritance jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise definition of 'Al-Kalalah' from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, establishes the primary condition for inheritance by collateral relatives in the absence of direct lineage. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith serves as the foundational textual evidence for interpreting the term 'Kalalah' in the Quranic verses of inheritance, clarifying that the specific rules for siblings apply only when no parents or children survive the deceased.
